body.statement: Can each candidate finite grammar produced while resolving the latent-lifting question pass the following bounded computational validation target on the binary independent-root kill instance: enumerate all \(4096\) deterministic response skeletons, every exact observed support of size at most four, and every query \(P_{A=a}(C=c)\); compare each candidate formula classification with constancy on the corresponding observational fiber; and compare each candidate obstruction with an explicit pair of full models having equal observed laws, the same exact support, unequal targets, and the latent-source architecture of \(G\)? Any candidate grammar failing one comparison is rejected.
body.justification: This finite computation is a falsifiable validation gate for architecture-preserving extension before a general grammar is accepted.
body.gap: No cited completeness proof checks simultaneous preservation of two independent sources, an exact structural-zero face, and a state-specific intervention on this graph.
body.consumer: The bounded audit rejects a candidate obstruction production before it is used in the general completeness proof or implementation.

obligation.what_is_open: Executing the requested exact comparison for every terminal classification of a concrete candidate grammar on the \(4096\)-skeleton independent-root instance.
obligation.obstruction: No candidate grammar, production list, formula classification, or local obstruction classification is defined in the frozen core. The finite skeleton list by itself does not determine the continuum of equal-observed-law fibers over independent root masses.
obligation.attempted: I reduced a fixed skeleton pair to exact polynomial equalities in the two pairs of Bernoulli root masses and the target inequality. This gives a bounded audit protocol once candidate productions exist, but there is presently no candidate output to accept or reject and a finite rational grid would not certify the required fibers.
obligation.partial_result: The audit domain is finite at the level of its \(4096\) deterministic skeletons and its finitely many support bitsets and queries.  For a fixed pair of skeletons, however, equality of the observed laws is a system of polynomial equations in the two independent Bernoulli root-mass pairs, not a comparison of skeleton support sets alone.  An exact audit can therefore enumerate the stated discrete cases and then decide, for every proposed terminal production, whether its polynomial fiber contains a compatible equal-law pair with unequal target.  No candidate production system is present in the frozen core, so no formula or obstruction classifications exist to compare in this round.
